illusioni.d: Over 70 optical illusions and interactive rooms: fun for all ages.

cappuccini.d: Chapels decorated with the bones of thousands of friars: macabre and unique in the world.

montemartini.d: Roman statues displayed among the turbines of an old power station.

serra_moresca.d: 19th-century greenhouse in Alhambra style, with coloured glass. Closed in July and August.

museo_luce.d: The physics of light told through hands-on installations.

welcome_rome.d: A multimedia journey through the city's 2,700 years: a great introduction.

barracco.d: Small collection of Egyptian, Assyrian, Greek and Roman sculpture.

museo_mura.d: Walk inside Porta San Sebastiano and along the Aurelian Walls.

lab_mente.d: In the former Santa Maria della Pietà asylum: moving and little known.

anime_purgatorio.d: A tiny collection of "imprints from the afterlife" inside a neo-Gothic church.
anime_purgatorio.n: Museum of the Souls of Purgatory

buco_serratura.d: St Peter's dome framed in the keyhole of the Knights of Malta.

coppede.d: Fairy-tale architecture mixing Art Nouveau, Gothic and medieval.

palazzo_valentini.d: Roman houses beneath a palace, brought back to life by multimedia projections.

case_celio.d: Frescoed Roman homes beneath a basilica.

galleria_spada.d: Famous for Borromini's false perspective: 9 metres that look like 35.

galleria_sciarra.d: A frescoed Art Nouveau courtyard hidden a few steps from Via del Corso.

maxxi.d: Contemporary art in the building designed by Zaha Hadid.

dreamers.d: Colourful immersive rooms designed for photos.

ikono.d: A sensory experience through themed rooms.

time_elevator.d: A 5D cinema with moving seats about the history of Rome, great for children.

colosseo.d: The symbol of Rome and the heart of the ancient city, all with one ticket.
colosseo.e: The Colosseum from outside, with the Arch of Constantine and the view over the Forum. Entry not included.

pantheon.d: The best-preserved Roman temple, with the largest concrete dome ever built.
pantheon.e: The facade of the Pantheon and Piazza della Rotonda with its fountain. Entry not included.

trevi.d: The world's most famous fountain. Free view from the square, €2 to go down close to the water.

navona.d: Baroque square with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.

spagna.d: The most famous staircase in Rome, with the Barcaccia fountain at its foot.
spagna.n: Spanish Steps and Trinità dei Monti

capitolini.d: The oldest public museum in the world, in the square designed by Michelangelo.
capitolini.n: Capitoline Museums and Piazza del Campidoglio
capitolini.fn: Piazza del Campidoglio and Forum terrace
capitolini.e: Michelangelo's Piazza del Campidoglio and the free terrace over the Roman Forum.

castel_santangelo.d: From Hadrian's mausoleum to papal fortress, with a panoramic terrace.
castel_santangelo.e: The castle seen from the Bridge of Angels and the riverside. Entry not included.

vittoriano.d: An imposing monument with free entry; the panoramic terrace costs €18.

fori_imperiali.d: A walk past the forums of Caesar, Augustus and Trajan, visible from the street.

ghetto.d: Europe's oldest Jewish quarter, among Roman ruins and Jewish-style artichokes.

popolo.d: A grand neoclassical square with its obelisk and twin churches.

campo_fiori.d: Market in the morning, nightlife in the evening, with the statue of Giordano Bruno.

bocca_verita.d: The legendary mask that bites the hands of liars.
bocca_verita.e: You can see the Mouth of Truth through the portico gate, even without going in.

torre_argentina.d: The sacred area where Caesar was killed, today also a cat sanctuary.

teatro_marcello.d: A Roman theatre with an inhabited palace built on top of it.

isola_tiberina.d: The Tiber's only island, linked by the oldest Roman bridge still in use.

circo_massimo.d: Antiquity's largest stadium, today a huge lawn.

ara_pacis.d: Augustus' altar in Richard Meier's glass pavilion.
ara_pacis.e: Augustus' altar seen through Richard Meier's glass pavilion.

musei_vaticani.d: One of the largest collections in the world, up to Michelangelo's Last Judgement. Skip-the-line online €25.

san_pietro.d: The largest church in Christendom, with Michelangelo's Pietà.

cupola.d: Lift plus 320 steps (€10) or 551 steps on foot (€8) to the most famous view of Rome.

grotte_vaticane.d: The tombs of the popes beneath the basilica.

necropoli.d: Guided visit to St Peter's tomb: book well in advance.

giardini_vaticani.d: Guided visit to the popes' gardens, booking only. From €20, €40 with the open bus.

ponte_santangelo.d: Bernini's bridge of angels, in front of the castle.

borgo_pio.d: Little streets beneath the secret corridor that led the popes to the castle.
borgo_pio.n: Borgo Pio and Passetto di Borgo

prati.d: An elegant late-19th-century district, great for shopping.
prati.n: Prati and Via Cola di Rienzo

laterano.d: The cathedral of Rome, mother of all churches in the world.

santa_maria_maggiore.d: 5th-century mosaics and a gilded ceiling made with the first gold from the Americas.

san_paolo.d: An immense basilica with portraits of every pope and a splendid cloister.

vincoli.d: Michelangelo's Moses and the chains of St Peter.

san_clemente.d: Three layers: a medieval church, a 4th-century basilica and a temple of Mithras. Excavations by booking.

santa_maria_trastevere.d: One of the oldest churches in Rome, with golden mosaics on the facade and apse.

san_luigi.d: Three Caravaggio masterpieces on the life of St Matthew, for free.

sant_ignazio.d: Andrea Pozzo's painted false dome: a mirror in the middle reveals the trick.

santa_maria_popolo.d: Two Caravaggios and the Chigi Chapel by Raphael and Bernini.

gesu.d: The Jesuits' Baroque masterpiece; every day at 5:30 pm the "machine" of St Ignatius' altar.

minerva.d: Rome's only Gothic church, with Bernini's little elephant in front.

scala_santa.d: The stairs Jesus is said to have climbed to Pilate: pilgrims go up on their knees.

vittoria.d: The Ecstasy of St Teresa, Bernini's masterpiece.

aracoeli.d: Reached by climbing 124 steps; inside, frescoes by Pinturicchio.

santa_cecilia.d: The statue of the saint carved as she was found, and a rare fresco by Cavallini.

santa_prassede.d: The Chapel of St Zeno, entirely covered in golden mosaics.

quattro_fontane.d: Borromini's masterpiece: an oval dome as big as one pillar of St Peter's.

sant_andrea_quirinale.d: Bernini's "pearl", a hundred metres from his rival Borromini's church.

santo_stefano_rotondo.d: A round 5th-century church with graphic frescoes of martyrs.

quattro_coronati.d: A fortified monastery with the Chapel of St Sylvester and a hidden cloister.

santa_sabina.d: A 5th-century basilica with its original wooden door and the Orange Garden next door.

tempietto_bramante.d: The jewel of the Renaissance, where tradition says Peter was crucified.

santa_maria_angeli.d: Michelangelo turned the Baths of Diocletian into a church; a meridian line on the floor.

sant_ivo.d: Borromini's spiral dome; usually open only on Sunday mornings.

san_lorenzo.d: A medieval basilica with a cloister, next to the Verano cemetery.

santa_costanza.d: A 4th-century mausoleum with still-pagan grape harvest mosaics.

chiostro_bramante.d: A Renaissance cloister hosting exhibitions, with a café overlooking Santa Maria della Pace.

cosma_damiano.d: A 6th-century apse mosaic and a large 18th-century Neapolitan nativity scene.

galleria_borghese.d: Bernini and Caravaggio in a Baroque villa. Booking required, 2-hour slots.

villa_borghese.d: Rome's most famous park: avenues, a lake with rowing boats, bike and rickshaw hire.

pincio.d: Views over Piazza del Popolo and the domes, stunning at sunset.

giardino_aranci.d: The most romantic sunset in Rome, among orange trees above the Tiber.

gianicolo.d: The widest view over the city; a cannon is fired at noon.

fontanone.d: The monumental Acqua Paola fountain, overlooking Trastevere.

terrazza_caffarelli.d: A terrace on the Capitoline Hill overlooking the rooftops and the Vittoriano.

parco_acquedotti.d: Arches of Roman aqueducts in open meadows: the Rome of "The Great Beauty".

appia_antica.d: The "queen of roads": Roman paving stones, tombs and countryside, on foot or by bike.

villa_doria_pamphilj.d: Rome's largest park, loved by locals for running and picnics.

villa_torlonia.d: Mussolini's villa: free park, Art Nouveau House of the Owls for €10.50.

roseto.d: Over a thousand varieties of roses, open only in spring.

villa_celimontana.d: A quiet park a stone's throw from the Colosseum, with an Egyptian obelisk.

villa_sciarra.d: A small romantic garden with fountains and statues, almost unknown to tourists.

villa_ada.d: A large natural park with a lake, a former royal residence.

caffarella.d: Roman countryside in the city: farms, nymphaea and ruins.

orto_botanico.d: A botanical garden at the foot of the Janiculum, with greenhouses and bamboo.

bioparco.d: Rome's zoo, ideal for those travelling with children.

villa_medici.d: Home of the French Academy: Renaissance gardens with guided tours.

zodiaco.d: The highest point in Rome, far from the centre: reached by bus or taxi.

domus_aurea.d: Nero's buried palace, with a VR headset showing the rooms as they were. Small groups, book early.

colosseo_sotterranei.d: A special tour where gladiators and beasts passed, with access to the arena.

caracalla.d: The most impressive baths of antiquity, less crowded than the Forum. Opera in summer.
caracalla.e: The imposing ruins of the baths seen from the avenue. Entry not included.

ostia_antica.d: A Pompeii 30 minutes away by train: streets, taverns, a theatre and intact houses.

palazzo_massimo.d: Frescoes from Livia's villa, the Boxer at Rest and extraordinary mosaics.

terme_diocleziano.d: Huge Roman baths with a cloister by Michelangelo.

palazzo_altemps.d: Ancient sculpture in a Renaissance palace, including the Ludovisi Throne.

crypta_balbi.d: How Rome changed from antiquity to the Middle Ages, layer by layer.

mercati_traiano.d: The "shopping mall" of ancient Rome, with a view down over the Forums.

carcere_mamertino.d: The prison where tradition says St Peter was held.

stadio_domiziano.d: The Roman stadium hidden beneath Piazza Navona, which explains its shape.

vicus_caprarius.d: Under Trevi, an ancient Roman house crossed by the water that feeds the fountain.

mausoleo_augusto.d: The round tomb of the first emperor, reopened after decades of restoration.
mausoleo_augusto.e: The round tomb of Augustus seen from the square.

san_callisto.d: The largest and most famous catacombs, with the crypt of the popes. Guided tour included.

domitilla.d: Catacombs with an underground basilica and early Christian frescoes. Guided tour included.

san_sebastiano.d: Catacombs with perfectly preserved Roman mausoleums.

priscilla.d: The oldest known image of the Madonna. Close to our properties.

cecilia_metella.d: The fortress-mausoleum that symbolises the Appian Way.

villa_quintili.d: A huge, almost deserted imperial villa, off the tourist trail.

cimitero_acattolico.d: The romantic cemetery of Keats and Shelley, in the shadow of a Roman pyramid.
cimitero_acattolico.n: Non-Catholic Cemetery and Pyramid of Cestius

monte_testaccio.d: A hill made entirely of broken amphorae: the rubbish dump of ancient Rome. Only on occasional guided tours.

trastevere.d: Cobbled lanes, ivy and trattorias: the most Roman district of Rome, at its best in the evening.

monti.d: The oldest district, now full of vintage shops, artisans and little squares.

testaccio.d: The district of genuine Roman cooking, with its covered market and street food.

via_margutta.d: The street of artists and of "Roman Holiday", with workshops and galleries.

piazza_mattei.d: A small Renaissance fountain in a hidden little square of the Ghetto.

garbatella.d: A 1920s garden city: cottages, courtyards and picture-postcard social housing.

pigneto.d: Pasolini's district, now murals, bars and alternative nightlife.

via_giulia.d: A dead-straight Renaissance street with noble palaces and the Farnese arch.

piazza_farnese.d: An elegant square with Michelangelo's palace, today the French Embassy.

via_coronari.d: The street of antique dealers, steps from Piazza Navona.

san_lorenzo_quartiere.d: The university district, murals and bars. A few steps from our properties.

eur.d: The rationalist city built for the 1942 Exposition, with the "Square Colosseum".

ostiense_street_art.d: Industrial archaeology and huge murals, from the Gasometer to the former wholesale markets.

tor_marancia.d: Twenty-two social housing blocks painted by international street artists.

governo_vecchio.d: Vintage shops and workshops between Navona and Chiesa Nuova.

quadraro.d: An open-air urban art museum in a working-class district of the Resistance.

porta_portese.d: Rome's most famous flea market: Sunday mornings only.

mercato_centrale.d: A food hall with the best artisan producers under one roof.

mercato_trionfale.d: The locals' covered market, steps from the Vatican Museums.

campagna_amica.d: Produce from Lazio's farmers, on Saturdays and Sundays.
campagna_amica.n: Campagna Amica farmers' market at Circus Maximus

cooking_class.d: Learn to make fresh pasta, tiramisù or pizza, then eat what you cooked. Usually €60-90.

food_tour.d: Guided tastings of supplì, pizza by the slice, cheese and gelato. Usually €60-90.
food_tour.n: Food tour in Trastevere or Testaccio

vespa_tour.d: Rome as in "Roman Holiday", with a driver or behind the wheel. Usually €80-150.

golf_cart.d: The historic centre without effort: ideal for those who walk little.

bici_appia.d: Rent a bike at the Appia Info Point and ride among tombs and Roman paving stones.

crociera_tevere.d: Rome seen from the river, also with dinner on board.

cinecitta.d: Visit Fellini's studios and the ancient Rome film sets.

explora.d: An interactive museum where children do everything themselves.

opera_caracalla.d: Open-air opera and ballet among the ruins of the baths. Summer only.
opera_caracalla.n: Opera at the Baths of Caracalla

tivoli.d: Two UNESCO sites in one day: Emperor Hadrian's villa and the garden of a hundred fountains.
tivoli.n: Tivoli: Villa d'Este and Hadrian's Villa

pompei.d: The city buried by Vesuvius. Frecciarossa to Naples then the Circumvesuviana: a long but unforgettable day.

firenze.d: The Frecciarossa gets you there in an hour and a half: the best of the Renaissance in one day.

orvieto.d: An Etruscan town on a tufa cliff, with one of the finest Gothic cathedrals in Italy and a maze of caves.

napoli.d: An hour and ten minutes by Frecciarossa to Italy's liveliest city, and its pizza.

castelli.d: Towns on volcanic hills: Frascati wine, Ariccia porchetta, Nemi strawberries and the papal palace.
castelli.no: The Papal Palace at Castel Gandolfo charges admission

tuscia.d: "The dying town" on its tufa spur and the garden of monstrous sculptures that enchanted Dalí. A car is needed.
tuscia.n: Civita di Bagnoregio and the Park of Monsters

assisi.d: The town of St Francis, with the basilica frescoed by Giotto.

cerveteri.d: A UNESCO Etruscan city of the dead, with house-shaped tombs. The Ladispoli seaside is nearby.

tarquinia.d: The most beautiful frescoed Etruscan tombs in the world, colours still vivid after 2,500 years.

ninfa.d: The "most romantic garden in the world" among the ruins of a medieval town. Open only on some days, by booking.

sperlonga.d: A white village above the sea with some of the best beaches in Lazio. Ideal in summer.

viterbo.d: The medieval city of the popes, with intact districts and free hot springs to bathe in.

bracciano.d: A medieval castle on a volcanic lake, with a lakeside walk and a lake-fish lunch.

subiaco.d: Monasteries clinging to the rock where St Benedict founded his order.

montecassino.d: St Benedict's abbey, destroyed and rebuilt after the 1944 battle.

mare_ostia.d: The Romans' beach, reachable with a city transport ticket. Summer only.

trastevere.d: The heart of the Roman evening: aperitivo in Piazza San Calisto, dinner in a trattoria, then the steps of Piazza Trilussa.

monti.d: Aperitivo in Piazza Madonna dei Monti among locals and tourists, then dinner around Via Panisperna.

campo_navona.d: Wine bars in Via del Governo Vecchio and Piazza del Fico, dinner near Navona, the evening in Campo de' Fiori.

ghetto.d: Roman-Jewish dinner: Jewish-style artichokes and fried cod fillets between Portico d'Ottavia and Via del Portico.

testaccio.d: The most genuine Roman cooking, from oxtail stew to cacio e pepe; then bars until late.

pigneto.d: An alternative pedestrian area, natural wines and craft beers. Close to our properties.

tridente.d: Elegant aperitivo and terraces with a view between Via Margutta and Piazza del Popolo.
tridente.n: Spanish Steps and Piazza del Popolo

prati.d: Refined aperitivo bars and quiet restaurants, perfect after a day at the Vatican.

san_lorenzo.d: The university district: cheap, lively, full of trattorias and pubs. A short walk from home.

ostiense.d: A former industrial area with bars, restaurants and clubs; Eataly for those who want everything in one place.

ponte_milvio.d: Young Romans' aperitivo spot, with the bridge of padlocks.

piazza_bologna.d: For a quiet evening near our properties: you will find our recommended places in the Eat section.
